key_insight: A hybrid cross-modal attention model combining mammograms and structured clinical data substantially improves early breast cancer detection in a low-resource African hospital setting.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support faster, more reliable triage where radiology expertise and data infrastructure are limited, while adapting better to local patient populations.
method: Trained a transformer-based cross-modal attention network on mammograms plus clinical variables.
Used a locally collected dataset of 2,560 mammograms from 1,024 patients across four Ethiopian referral hospitals.
Compared performance against image-only baselines and assessed robustness to low-quality images.
evidence_signal: In local validation, the model achieved 97.8% accuracy, 97.2% sensitivity, 98.3% specificity, and an AUC of 0.987, with only 3.2% degradation on low-quality images.
watch_item: Results come from a specific Ethiopian dataset, so broader generalizability and real-world workflow performance still need external validation.
paper_title: Hybrid Cross-Modal Attention Network for Early Breast Cancer Detection in Low-Resource Clinical Settings
